attribution.interpretation: P023 preserved global uniqueness for all 179 realized rows and filled seven of eight cells. The remaining gap cannot be explained mainly by fallback readiness failures; strict global identity exclusion and scarce early-STAR identity availability remain the dominant resource constraint.

successor.name: Cross-Era Clustered-Identity Development Contract
successor.recommended_scope: Return to the P013 identity×non-overlapping-window×role development model. Require 24 distinct identities inside each Era×Board cell, allow the same economic identity to appear across non-overlapping era cells with explicit cluster provenance, preserve identity-global exclusion for preserved evaluation, and never count repeated cross-era identities as independent evidence. A separately frozen technical successor may process only previously skipped global-conflict candidates needed to fill remaining same-cell deficits; completed readiness reads must not be rerun.

claim_ceiling: P023 shows that primary-first realized-identity replacement reaches 179 globally unique admission-ready development cases and closes only on a 13-case early-STAR deficit. It does not establish Stage1/12 semantic quality and does not authorize weakening preserved identity independence, opening newer years, dropping STAR, or beginning semantic review.
